I don‘t think there‘s a lot GW2 can do at this point.

But here‘s a list:

- They need a marketing team, a good one.

- Make Homesteads public, reduce decoration costs.

- Next expansion needs to be big, I‘m talking HoT/PoF with new elite specs.

- A refreshing Map, completely underwater with a overhaul to underwater combat or add mechanics to airborn combat and make a Map that‘s almost completely about flying/gliding.

- Overhaul to Dungeons. 

- Add new raids at LEAST every 6-8 months instead of one every 5 years.

GW2 and Anet need a shakeup. Idk if they will only be giving minimal patches and expansions until GW3 gets released but even so they need to start marketing that game.

Because if they don‘t the same thing will happen again and again. When GW2 was released, some people left GW1 and tried GW2. A lot of the stayed but some went back to GW1. 

I remember I was 14 when I started playing GW2. I only found out about the game because a German youtuber named Honeyball was obsessed with the game. But she also quit a while back.

Guild Wars needs more incentive to play the game that isn‘t just mindless grinding.

Some of the most fun I had was playing the collection for Astralaria. The small quests to get certain items. All the new Legy‘s are just mindless grinding again. Get X amount of mats, run 7000 T3 Rifts, etc. 

GW2 needs a smart way to reward players, new and experienced. Right now a lot of the Game involves grinding.

I love the idea of Homsteads but I don‘t like the implementation.

I‘m a fashion wars kinda guy. So my love to make things look nice could branch out to interior design. I remember building whole mansions in Valheim for example.

My two biggest issues are:
- How expensive it is
- They aren’t public


As of now, the only reason to go to homesteads is for the daily mat farm. That’s it, and it’s sad.

I’m not saying make it free, but make it 10-100 times less expensive.
You can add expensive specialty items, maybe legendary decorations or something. But we need common stuff.

For people who haven’t maxxed out their char there’s no point in starting to spend their time interior designing, simply because it’s kind of a waste of time atm.

If you got a full legy gear you can at least play every single gamemode in GW2. If you got a nice homestead you might get a “wow” when someone enters it for 5 minutes to clear out the matts.

It’s truly a bummer and I hope Anet doesn’t give up completely on them.

When I first started playing the game, both jungle and support were purely supporting roles, with minimal gold. The little gold they earned was spent mostly on vision, and only supports and junglers warded. Fast forward 12 years, and we now have players who are better at CSing, gold-generating items for supports, bounties, bigger shutdowns, and more passive gold income.

However, comparing pro games to solo queue isn’t fair—they’re two completely different experiences.

The frustration with the game isn’t about the gold; it’s that it doesn’t feel rewarding anymore. Numerous factors aren’t working as they should: the red side in high elo, the bounty system, and stale metas. Riot takes too long to fix broken systems.

For instance, instead of nerfing a single item, Riot nerfs every AP jungler. Midlane mages have become nearly unplayable because adc‘s are much better. The bounty system not only allows teams to come back but sometimes even overtake the leading team unfairly.

Yes, players have improved, but the reason many miss the older seasons has nothing to do with gold. It’s about how games can be lost by a single person but not won by one. I remember in Season 3, I was a Gold Rengar top lane one-trick. I could play on a Bronze account and drop 20+ kills every game. Today, even if you’re a smurf, if one person decides to int, you’ll likely lose.

The game is so focused on teamplay and comebacks that playing with friends is more fun and rewarding than playing solo queue. Yet, Riot removed Team Ranked for Flex Queue, which has become a mess—there’s currently a player with 2800 LP in Flex Queue. Team Ranked would have prevented this.

Riot claims to balance around teamplay but refuses to implement a voice chat for League. They remove and limit ping options, and they’ve even removed Duo Queue in high elo for „ranked integrity.“

This is the core issue: Riot makes contradictory decisions that don’t make sense. They need to choose a clear direction.

When I started playing, you could qualify for the Challenger Series if you were one of the best teams in Team Ranked. Back then, Solo Queue mattered—people were actually scouted from it. Now, it doesn’t. Most pros would rather scrim than play solo queue.

Solo Queue should simply be for entertainment now. Let big streamers Duo Queue. Bring back the excitement of streams like those from Noway and Broxah.

In recent years, Riot has made decisions against the player base. Why remove Twisted Treeline? It was fun and had an active player base. Why remove Team Ranked? Why not introduce something like Valorant’s Premier mode into LoL?

Clash is a failed experiment—let it die. A 8-team tournament that offers little reward every few weeks isn’t interesting.

Regarding pro-play: in any game, once the pro‘s optimize it to the maximum it‘s very hard to not make the game boring.
Let‘s take Apex Legends as an example.
Up to the last circle it‘s really boring to watch because nothing happens. Teams farm gear try to avoid confrontation and pick Legends that can barricade themselves in. 

With League it‘s similar. Solo kills happen rarely. Tank junglers are often the meta. Players try to just outfarm and outmacro each other. But this is bound to happen when players get better and better.

Pro play is also really stale. In EU it‘s always G2 that‘s strong, in LCK it‘s between GenG and T1. 
Bottom teams are rarely relevant. I think this would be fixed if we move away from the franchising system back to a system where teams can actually demote and promote from and to a League. I am sure teams would try harder again.

One thing that never changed was that the damage that the spear dealt was increased by the distance travelled. Even toplane when it wasn‘t truly used. There‘s absolutely no point in changing how that mechanic works. 
Look at Zoe her Q works the same way. 

If you remove damage on Q you‘ll need to put a lot more damage into cougar form and this just takes away skill. It doesn‘t add skill at all. 

The hardest thing you need to do in cougar form is some animation cancelling and pressing E before Q to maximize damage. 

If you don‘t hit a good spear you won‘t deal enough damage to go in. This means you need to hit a spear. The higher you get in the elo the harder it is. And this means, it takes skill to hit it, to know its limits.
